Headphones in OGGB: A Study of Student Habits at UoA

Mea van Rooyen

What’s going on with this data?

This data was collected through observing students in the OGGB at the University of Auckland. Each observation recorded the headphone type worn, the student’s observed gender, their task, and the time of day.

Who is wearing what?

Female students in the OGGB appear to favour headphones, while male students show a noticeably higher proportion of earphones. This suggests that headphone preference may actually differ between genders, possibly reflecting differences in comfort or style/aesthetics.

A stacked bar chart showing the proportion of female vs male students using earphones vs headphones. Female students appear to favour earphones while male students show a higher proportion of headphones.

What headphone type is preferred with different tasks?

Studying is by far the most common activity observed in the OGGB (surprise!), and headphones are the dominant choice across all tasks. Earphones appear just as popular among students who are chatting, which may suggest they are used more socially than for focused work.

A grouped bar chart showing the headphone type counts vs tasks (chatting, eating, studying, other). Studying is the most common task, with earphones dominating

What task is most popular at different times?

Studying activity peaks during the late morning hours, which aligns with typical class schedules at UoA. Chatting and eating are distributed more evenly across the day, suggesting the OGGB serves different purposes depending on the time you visit. I thought it was interesting that the moment studying dipped in density, chatting spiked. It also made sense that eating and other acitivities aligned because students typically scroll on phones, or walk, when they are eating their lunch/snacks.

A density plot showing the distribution of tasks across hours of the day. Studying appears to peak in the late morning, while chatting and eating are spread more evenly throughout the day
